source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Animal Diversity II: Phylum Chordata
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: A dorsal hollow nerve cord, notochord and pharyngeal gill slits together diagnose the phylum
questions.explanation: These three (plus a post-anal tail) are the fundamental chordate characters.

questions.stem: In urochordates such as Ascidia, the notochord is present
options: throughout life in the entire body
only in the tail of the larva
questions.explanation: Urochordate larvae are tadpole-like with a tail notochord; the adult is sessile and loses it.

questions.stem: Jawless, eel-like vertebrates with a suctorial mouth are placed in
questions.explanation: Petromyzon (lamprey) and Myxine (hagfish) are cyclostomes (Agnatha).

questions.stem: Cartilaginous fishes typically possess
options: an operculum covering gills and a swim bladder
placoid scales and claspers in males
cycloid scales and a bony endoskeleton
questions.explanation: Chondrichthyes (e.g. Scoliodon) have placoid scales, exposed gill slits and pelvic claspers in males.

questions.stem: An air bladder (swim bladder) that regulates buoyancy is characteristic of
questions.explanation: Most bony fishes have a swim bladder; cartilaginous fishes lack it and must swim to avoid sinking.

questions.stem: Moist skin that assists cutaneous respiration is a hallmark of
questions.explanation: Amphibians have glandular skin without scales (in living forms) and often respire partly through the skin.

questions.stem: Dry cornified skin with epidermal scales and typically a three-chambered heart occur in
questions.explanation: Reptiles are terrestrial amniotes with scales; crocodiles are an exception with a four-chambered heart.

questions.stem: Pneumatic bones and a covering of feathers are features of
questions.explanation: Birds have hollow bones, feathers, a four-chambered heart and are homoiothermic.

questions.stem: Mammary glands and a covering of hair diagnose the class
questions.explanation: Mammals nourish young with milk and have hair; they are homoiothermic with a four-chambered heart.

questions.stem: Vertebrates with jaws are collectively placed in
questions.explanation: Gnathostomata includes fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals; cyclostomes are agnathans.

questions.stem: Branchiostoma (Amphioxus) is a cephalochordate because the notochord
options: is confined to the larval tail
extends from head to tail throughout life
is replaced by a vertebral column in the adult
is absent and replaced by a stomochord
questions.explanation: In Cephalochordata the notochord persists the length of the body for life; there is no cranium.

questions.stem: Which fish is an osteichthyan with an operculum?
questions.explanation: Catla is a bony carp; sting ray, great white shark and sawfish are cartilaginous fishes.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect match of vertebrate and unique feature.
questions.explanation: Salamander is an amphibian with moist skin, not feathers. Platypus is a monotreme; ostrich is a ratite; crocodiles have a four-chambered heart.

questions.stem: The notochord of chordates is a
options: dorsal rod of vacuolated cells beneath the nerve cord
questions.explanation: The notochord is a flexible dorsal supporting rod; in vertebrates it is largely replaced by the vertebral column.

questions.stem: Salpa, Doliolum and Ascidia are
questions.explanation: These tunicates have a cellulose-like tunic; the notochord is larval and caudal.

questions.stem: Petromyzon is a marine cyclostome that migrates to fresh water to
questions.explanation: Sea lampreys are anadromous: they spawn in rivers; the larva is an ammocoete.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a cartilaginous fish?
questions.explanation: Trygon (sting ray) is chondrichthyan; flying fish, seahorse and magur are bony fishes.

questions.stem: Cycloid or ctenoid scales and a terminal mouth are typical of
questions.explanation: Bony fishes usually have overlapping cycloid/ctenoid scales, an operculum and a terminal mouth.

questions.stem: Ichthyophis, Hyla and Salamandra are
questions.explanation: Limbless caecilian, tree frog and salamander are amphibians.

questions.stem: Chelone, Naja, Calotes and Crocodilus belong to
questions.explanation: Turtle, cobra, garden lizard and crocodile are reptiles with dry scaly skin.

questions.stem: Which bird is flightless?
questions.explanation: Struthio (ostrich) is a ratite; pigeon, parrot and crow are flying birds.

questions.stem: Macropus, Pteropus, Balaenoptera and Ornithorhynchus are all
questions.explanation: Kangaroo, bat, blue whale and platypus are mammals (marsupial, flying, aquatic and oviparous respectively).

questions.stem: Pisces in the older grouping of Gnathostomata includes
questions.explanation: Jawed fishes comprise cartilaginous and bony classes; cyclostomes are agnathous.

questions.stem: Which statement about amphibians is incorrect?
options: Heart is three-chambered (two atria, one ventricle)
Fertilisation is usually external in frogs
questions.explanation: Amphibians are poikilothermic (cold-blooded); only birds and mammals are typically homoiothermic.

questions.stem: In birds, the alimentary canal has a crop and gizzard. Additional flight adaptations include
options: teeth on both jaws and a urinary bladder
air sacs, keeled sternum and one functional ovary in females
questions.explanation: Air sacs aid ventilation; a keeled sternum anchors flight muscles; most female birds have a single left ovary.

questions.stem: Which pairing of protochordate character is wrong?
options: Urochordata — notochord in larval tail only
Both groups — marine protochordates without a cranium
Urochordata — vertebral column in the adult tunicate
questions.explanation: Tunicates never develop vertebrae; Vertebrata is a separate subphylum with a cranium and usually a vertebral column.
